card.title: IWO JIMA
card.text: Iwo Jima was a heavily fortified Japanese island during WWII.
card.flavorText: Iwo Jima was a crucial part of Japan’s inner defensive line. In 1944, Lieutenant General Tadamichi Kuribayashi abandoned traditional beach defenses, instead transforming the volcanic island into a fortress with 18 kilometers of underground tunnels, caves, and bunkers. This extensive network allowed his troops to survive heavy bombardments and reoccupy cleared positions. When US Marines landed on 19 February 1945, Kuribayashi withheld fire until the beaches were crowded with men and equipment, sparking a brutal five-week struggle against deeply entrenched defenders. Although Mount Suribachi fell on 23 February, fierce resistance continued across the northern defenses. The island was officially declared secure on 26 March, though Japanese holdouts remained hidden in the caves.
